items.title: 6.1.4 Equation of a Circle with Given End points of a Diameter (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Book p. 167: equation of the circle on the diameter with ends A(x1, y1), B(x2, y2) using the right angle in a semicircle, Figure 6.4; Do You Know? box

blocks.text: Kabhi sawal mein centre aur radius nahin diye hote, balke diameter ke do kinare (end points) diye hote hain. Aaj hum aisi surat mein seedha circle ki equation likhna seekhenge, aur is ke liye geometry ki ek purani aur khoobsurat baat istemal karenge. Sochiye aap ke paas ek rassi hai jis ke dono sire do kheeliyon A aur B par bandhe hain, aur aap rassi ke beech mein ek kona (corner) bana kar, use hamesha 90 degree rakhte hue ghumate hain. Woh kona jis raaste par chalega, woh AB ko diameter maan kar bana circle hai. Yahi idea is sabaq ki jaan hai.

blocks.alt: Pale yellow panel par cyan circle, centre O magenta X aur Y axes ke origin par. AB x-axis par diameter hai: baayen A(x1, y1), daayen B(x2, y2). Circle ka point P(x, y) magenta lines se A aur B se jura hai, aur P par right angle (90 darje) ka nishan hai.
blocks.caption: Figure 6.4: the angle APB in a semicircle is a right angle (original drawing after the textbook's Figure 6.4)

blocks.text:
Maan lijiye \(A(x_{1}, y_{1})\) aur \(B(x_{2}, y_{2})\) diameter ke end points hain, aur \(P(x, y)\) circle par koi bhi point hai. Plane geometry se hum jaante hain ke diameter circle ke kisi bhi point par right angle banata hai (semicircle mein angle 90 degree hota hai). Is liye
\[\angle APB = 90^{\circ}\]
Yani lines \(\overline{AP}\) aur \(\overline{BP}\) ek doosre par perpendicular hain.
\(\overline{AP}\) ki slope \(m_{1} = \frac{y - y_{1}}{x - x_{1}}\) hai aur \(\overline{BP}\) ki slope \(m_{2} = \frac{y - y_{2}}{x - x_{2}}\) hai (slope = y ka farq / x ka farq).
Do perpendicular lines ki slopes ka product \(-1\) hota hai, \(m_{1} \cdot m_{2} = -1\). Is liye:
\[\dfrac{y - y_{1}}{x - x_{1}} \cdot \dfrac{y - y_{2}}{x - x_{2}} = -1\]
Fractions khatam karne ke liye dono sides ko \((x - x_{1})(x - x_{2})\) se multiply karte hain:
\[(y - y_{1})(y - y_{2}) = -(x - x_{1})(x - x_{2})\]
Minus wala term left side par le aayein to:

blocks.text_alt: (x minus x1)(x minus x2) plus (y minus y1)(y minus y2) equals 0

blocks.text: Yahi circle ki required equation hai. Is ko 'diameter form' bhi kehte hain.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
\(\angle APB = 90^{\circ}\) kyun? Yeh Class IX/X ka theorem hai: 'semicircle mein bana angle right angle hota hai'. Yani circle ka har point \(P\) diameter \(AB\) ko 90 degree par dekhta hai. Perpendicular hone ki sharat \(m_{1}m_{2} = -1\) is geometric baat ko equation mein badal deti hai. Yeh geometry aur algebra ki dosti ki behtareen misaal hai.
Ek bareek nukta: jab \(P\) bilkul \(A\) ya \(B\) par ho (ya \(\overline{AP}\) vertical ho) to slope define hi nahin hoti. Magar aakhri equation mein koi fraction nahin, aur woh in points par bhi sach hai: \(x = x_{1}\), \(y = y_{1}\) rakhein to dono products zero ho jate hain. Is liye aakhri equation circle ke har point ko shamil karti hai.
Isi circle tak doosra raasta bhi hai: centre = \(AB\) ka mid-point, radius = \(|AB|\) ka aadha; phir standard form. Dono tareeqe ek hi equation dete hain; diameter form bas tez hai.

blocks.title: Do You Know?
blocks.text: Ek diye hue perimeter (ghere ki lambai) ke saath tamaam band shaklon mein circle ka area sab se zyada hota hai.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text: Is 'Do You Know?' ka roz marra wala matlab: agar aap ke paas ek rassi ho aur us se zameen ka zyada se zyada hissa gherna ho, to rassi ko circle ki shakal mein bichhaiye. Isi liye bohat si cheezein, jaise pani ki tankiyan aur pipes, gol banayi jati hain: kam material mein zyada jagah.

blocks.title: Hamari taraf se misaal
blocks.text:
(Yeh hamari misaal hai, kitab ki nahin.) Diameter ke end points \(A(1, 2)\) aur \(B(5, -4)\) hon to circle?
\[(x - 1)(x - 5) + (y - 2)(y + 4) = 0\]
\[x^{2} - 6x + 5 + y^{2} + 2y - 8 = 0\]
\[x^{2} + y^{2} - 6x + 2y - 3 = 0\]
Tasdeeq: centre \((3, -1)\) bilkul \(AB\) ka mid-point hai \(\left(\frac{1 + 5}{2}, \frac{2 - 4}{2}\right)\); radius \(\sqrt{9 + 1 + 3} = \sqrt{13}\), aur \(|AB|\) ka aadha \(\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{16 + 36} = \sqrt{13}\). Dono barabar!

blocks.title: Khud sochiye
blocks.text: Kya \(x^{2} + y^{2} = 25\) ko diameter form mein likh sakte hain? (Haan: diameter ke kinare \((-5, 0)\) aur \((5, 0)\) lein: \((x + 5)(x - 5) + y \cdot y = 0\), yani \(x^{2} - 25 + y^{2} = 0\).)

blocks.title: Yaad rakhne wali baatein
blocks.text:
1. Diameter ke kinare \((x_{1}, y_{1})\), \((x_{2}, y_{2})\): \((x - x_{1})(x - x_{2}) + (y - y_{1})(y - y_{2}) = 0\).
2. Yeh semicircle ke right angle (\(90^{\circ}\)) aur \(m_{1}m_{2} = -1\) se aati hai.
3. Centre diameter ka mid-point hai aur radius us ki lambai ka aadha.

blocks.title: Aam ghaltiyan
blocks.text:
1. Joriyan mila dena: \(x\) ke saath \(x_{1}, x_{2}\) aur \(y\) ke saath \(y_{1}, y_{2}\); \((x - x_{1})(y - y_{1})\) kabhi nahin.
2. Negative coordinates mein sign ki ghalti: kinara \((5, -4)\) ho to bracket \((y + 4)\) banegi.
3. Right side par \(r^{2}\) likh dena: diameter form mein right side hamesha 0 hoti hai.
